title: Circular Array Loop Detection
description:
You are given a circular array `nums` of non-zero integers representing an implicit linked list of length `n`, where index `i` points to index `((i + nums[i]) % n + n) % n`.

Return `true` if there exists a cycle in `nums` such that:
- Every step in the cycle moves in the **same direction** (either all `nums[idx] > 0` or all `nums[idx] < 0`), and
- The cycle contains **more than one** distinct index (no self-loops of length 1).

Otherwise, return `false`. Aim for `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
hints: Run Floyd's fast and slow pointers from each unvisited starting index, stopping immediately if direction changes or a 1-step self-loop is encountered.

To guarantee O(n) total time with O(1) extra space, whenever a search from index `i` fails to find a valid cycle, walk the same-direction path from `i` and zero out all visited cells so they are never explored again.

examples.explanation: Indices 0 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0 form a forward cycle of length 3 with all positive values.
Every negative index jumps to index 5 (+6) causing a sign change, and index 5 jumps to itself (a length-1 self-loop), so no valid cycle exists.
Indices 3 -> 4 -> 3 form a forward cycle of length 2 with all positive values.
